- Management claims its services and products command premium value due to their uniqueness (Board's Report, Nature of Business)
- Stated ability to leverage its own experience and goodwill to penetrate deeper into its segments (Board's Report, Future Outlook)
- Access to a promoter-linked group — Jonjua Air Limited, HSJONJUA AEROINFRA Private Limited and HSJONJUA INNOVATEAGRO Private Limited share the same promoters, and the Chairman cites working with other group companies as a growth driver
- GST structure favours the business: publishing of books and agriculture are Nil-rated, exports Zero-rated and brochures at 5%, which the MD&A says gives the Company huge leverage
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Currency movement — MD&A 'Opportunities & Threats, Risks & Concerns' states plainly that 'Currency movement can have significant impact on the operations of the Company'. The business is oriented to service exports and printed-book exports, so rupee moves hit realisations directly and the AR discloses no hedging.
- Global trade tensions — The same MD&A paragraph flags that 'growth of global trade tensions ... will impact the operations of the Company'. The stated outlook rests on the export thrust of the government, so a deterioration in trade conditions removes the Company's main cited tailwind.
- Change in tax structure, particularly GST rates — Management flags 'change in tax structure' as impacting operations, and separately says the Company 'will have huge leverage with the lower rates of GST' because publishing of books and agriculture are Nil-rated, exports Zero-rated and brochures at 5%. The economics of the business therefore depend on a concessional rate structure that can be changed by policy.
- Policy / regulatory and natural-calamity exposure outside management's control — The Cautionary Statement enumerates the factors that could make a significant difference to operations: 'climatic and economic conditions affecting demand and supply, Government regulations, taxations, and natural calamities over which the Company does not have any direct control'. Climatic exposure is material given the agriculture vertical.
- Single-activity revenue concentration — The MGT-9 principal-business-activities table shows one line — 'Sale of goods of any nature including intangible goods, shares and printed books' (NIC 4799) — at 98% of total turnover. Effectively the entire top line sits in one activity bucket, so the diversification described in the Board's Report is intent rather than realised mix.
- Very small organisation executing a broad diversification agenda — The MD&A states manpower strength as on 31 March 2026 was 6, while the Board's Report commits the Company to forays into digital and paper book lending, Aviation and Agro consultancy, Technology and Distressed Assets. Execution and key-person dependence are structural at this headcount.
- Dependence on promoter-controlled group entities — The Chairman names working with other group companies as the growth driver, and the Ind AS-24 note lists Jonjua Air Limited, HSJONJUA AEROINFRA Private Limited and HSJONJUA INNOVATEAGRO Private Limited — all sharing the Company's promoters — as entities with substantial control, with purchases, sales of goods/shares, trade-name and trade-secret transfers, deposits and loans flowing between them. Revenue quality and pricing are therefore not fully arm's-length.
- Sharp fall in promoter shareholding and promoter-funded indebtedness — The MGT-9 shows promoter and promoter-group holding falling from 44.10% to 28.67% during the year via a transfer of 23,65,012 shares (-15.43 percentage points), while the indebtedness statement shows the Company's year-end borrowing is entirely unsecured amounts 'payable to directors/promoter and promoter group'. Declining promoter skin-in-the-game alongside reliance on promoter funding is a structural governance exposure.

RPT dealings comprise sale of goods or services (printed books and unlisted shares) and sale of continuous business trade secret. Not disclosed as a subsidiary, JV or associate.
- Harjinder Singh Jonjua — related party: Managing Director / promoter. RPT dealings comprise purchase of goods including library books, purchase of shares, salary, purchase of intangibles, interest paid, loan through bank account, agriculture expenses/rent, sale of unlisted shares, original content copyright and liquidated damages received.

- Foray into new ventures: digital and paper book lending, Aviation and Agro consultancy services, Technology and Distressed Assets.

outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: The annual report discloses no plant, capacity addition, commissioning or ramp-up programme — Jonjua Overseas is an asset-light trading and services company (manpower strength of 6 as on 31 March 2026) operating from a registered office at 545, Jubilee Walk, Sector 70, Mohali, Punjab. Expansion is framed entirely as new business verticals rather than physical capex: the Board's Report states the Company intends to foray into new ventures involving digital and paper book lending, Aviation and Agro consultancy services, Technology and Distressed Assets, and is looking for new opportunities in Service Exports, Printed Books, Corporate Consultancy, Aviation, Book lending, Agriculture and Technology. The Chairman adds that, apart from existing verticals, the Company is looking at working with other group companies (Jonjua Air Limited, HSJONJUA AEROINFRA Private Limited and HSJONJUA INNOVATEAGRO Private Limited, which share its promoters) and is increasing its range of services and goods to widen geographical coverage. No project names, timelines or rupee quantum are given, and the capital-commitments disclosure shows NIL contracts remaining to be executed on capital account at both 31.03.2026 and 31.03.2025.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Export thrust of the present government together with political stability makes the industry outlook positive and, per management, leaves the Company well placed to tap the opportunity going forward.
- GST structure is a stated tailwind: publishing of books and agriculture are Nil-rated, exports Zero-rated and publication of brochures placed at 5% — management says the Company 'will have huge leverage with the lower rates of GST'.
- Government is promoting last-mile connectivity in aviation, cited as the backdrop for the Company's aviation-linked ambitions.
- Eased FDI approval mechanism — the Ministry of Commerce and Industry has removed Department of Revenue approval and mandated clearance of proposals within 10 weeks of application.
- India's IT/BPM industry backdrop cited by management: India is the world's largest sourcing destination, employing nearly four million people, with the IT and BPM industry expected to grow to US$350 billion by 2026, and India's IT services roughly 3-4 times cheaper than the US.
- Stated headwinds to the outlook: currency movement can have a significant impact on operations, and growth of global trade tensions and change in tax structure will impact operations.
